Neuroblastoma is included because it commonly causes bone pain (especially in legs/pelvis), fever, pallor/fatigue (from marrow metastases or anemia), and bruising (due to thrombocytopenia or DIC); GD2 positivity—though not yet tested—is a known immunophenotypic feature of neuroblastoma, making it a strong consideration despite extramedullary origin. Aplastic anemia explains fatigue and bruising (pancytopenia) and may cause low-grade fever, but does not cause bone pain—making it unlikely without additional evidence like reticulocytopenia or hypocellular marrow; confidence is lowest among top five.
